---
title: Reproducing the project
---

## Commands

`make sync` restores the Python environment from `uv.lock`. `make check` runs
Black, isort, flake8, and pytest. `make ci-docker` runs the same checks using the
standard `python:3.14-slim` image, without modifying the mounted checkout.

```sh
make fetch
make prepare AS_OF=2026-10-26
make compare
make publish
make site
```

`AS_OF` defaults to the current UTC date; supply it explicitly for reproducibility.
`DATA_DIR` defaults to `data/raw/cricsheet/odis`. Preparation can also read the
existing local `data/odis` YAML directory. Numeric filenames are Cricsheet match
IDs; mixing two representations of the same ID is an error.

The website is rendered with Quarto 1.10.19 in CI. `QUARTO` can point to a local
binary. The homepage includes the README automatically. Rendering does not acquire
data, execute the exploratory notebooks, or refit models. A post-render check
verifies local links and assets. Before rendering, saved publication checksums
are verified. Format pages and the coverage table are generated automatically
from the saved rankings and manifest. The publication is included in the repository so CI and readers can
render it without fetching match data or estimating models.

`make compare` reads the prepared tables and verifies their hashes. It runs the
specified three models on 2023–2025 annual holdouts, with separate gender fits and
three- and five-year training windows. `MODEL_ARGS` can override years/windows
for an explicitly exploratory run. See the [specification](lineup_experiment.qmd).

`make publish` verifies saved analysis files and copies them into a publication
with generated tables and download links. Changed analysis files fail validation
before the preceding publication is replaced. Predictions, paired losses, tuning
scores, coefficients, calibration, diagnostics, and source provenance are retained.
Publication also ranks the saved player coefficients within each competition,
model, window, and cutoff. It generates the ranking page and `rankings.csv` without
refitting the model. Publication code hashes are separate from the preserved
analysis code hashes.

## Rankings by format

After preparing ODIs, acquire and prepare the other two international formats:

```sh
make fetch FORMAT=Test
make prepare FORMAT=Test AS_OF=2026-10-26
make fetch FORMAT=T20I
make prepare FORMAT=T20I AS_OF=2026-10-26 PREPARE_ARGS="--since 2021-10-27"
make rankings AS_OF=2026-10-26
```

`FORMAT` selects the official archive and format-specific default directories.
The general `--since` preparation option filters by match start date and records
excluded files with their hashes. Here it sets the T20 input to the five-year
ranking window, excluding an older identity conflict documented in the
[specification](format_rankings.qmd). Update that boundary when changing the cutoff.
Included matches still undergo strict identity checks. Ranking refuses prepared
inputs that omit part of the requested window.

`make rankings` fits the six cohorts and replaces `out/release/current/` only
once all fits succeed. It saves an all-player CSV, six format/gender CSVs,
reconstructible model parameters, preparation manifests, the specification, and
code/output hashes. Ranking cutoffs and tuning split IDs are recorded. Models are
fitted during this command; website rendering only checks and displays saved files.
The CLI accepts `--specification` when running outside the source checkout.

## Layout

| Location | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `data/raw/cricsheet/odis/` | Downloaded archive, JSON matches, and acquisition receipt |
| `data/build/odis/` | Validated match, participant, and identity tables with manifest |
| `src/player_value/` | Acquisition, preparation, CLI, and website checks |
| `tests/` | Synthetic fixtures and behavior tests |
| `experiments/war/` | Preserved exploratory notebooks and results |
| `out/analysis/lineup/` | Saved fits' coefficients, forecasts, tuning, and evaluation |
| `out/release/current/` | Five-year rankings by format, model parameters, and provenance |
| `out/release/lineup/` | Verified research publication and generated summary |
| `docs/` | Website source and research specifications |
| `out/site/` | Rendered website |

Additional models will keep their own results under `out/analysis/` and verified
publication tables under `out/release/`. The format-ranking command publishes rolling-window associations. Dynamic
current-strength and WAR models remain future work.

## Prepared tables

`matches.csv` has one row per match. Dates, gender, format, teams, venue, toss,
outcome, delivery count, and lineup eligibility are preserved. `team_a` and
`team_b` are alphabetical labels, not home/away designations. Boolean flags are
0/1. Empty cells mean missing or not applicable, not zero.

`participants.csv` has one row per match, team, and player ID, retaining the
source's player name. `players.csv` has one row per stable ID, the latest observed
name, and the first and last appearance dates within the prepared sample.

`manifest.json` records the cutoff, source-file hashes and exclusions, counts by
gender, preparation-code hash, output hashes, and the acquisition receipt when
available. Existing local downloads without a receipt are labeled with a null
receipt; preparation does not invent a retrieval date. A cutoff filters match
dates but does not recreate the source data as they existed on that date.

Acquisition and preparation build a temporary directory before replacing their
destination. Errors preserve the previous successful stage. If an interrupted
installation leaves a `.previous` directory, inspect and resolve it before rerunning.
Raw downloads, build products, and analysis intermediates are ignored by Git.
Verified publication files under `out/release/` are intended for version control.

## Repository transition

This project continues `outside-edge/war` under the name `outside-edge/player_value`.
The existing history is retained. The original artifacts have a checksum relocation
record in `experiments/relocations.csv`; their numerical contents are unchanged.
The local checkout directory can retain its existing name without affecting any
commands. There is no dependency on `../side_order`.

CI checks the package, builds its distribution, and renders the website. The Pages
workflow deploys the website after checks pass on pushes to main, and can also
be triggered manually. Scheduled rating updates and player-value releases remain gated on the
model-validation criteria in [Model comparisons](models.qmd).
